mechanisms.behavior: Own-edition item12 identifies left assembly500-6543-12-ND. Exact firmware button2 causes public coil2 with255/44/0 and virtual47/48 in bounded runtime. That route is not joined to this physical assembly without own electrical evidence.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Own-edition item13 identifies right assembly500-6543-02-ND. Exact firmware button3 causes public coil3 with255/44/0 and virtual45/46 in bounded runtime. Winding count, physical connector route and timing remain unresolved.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Own item18 establishes a three-bank in-line assembly500-1004-00. Firmware labels DROP TARGET1-3 at41/42/43 and reset output8 are candidate routes, not a verified electrical join to this assembly. No successful reset, physical linkage, home state, timing or jam recovery was exercised.
mechanisms.label: Three-bank in-line assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Own item24 identifies kicker511-1013-00. Parts item6 prints trough511-1022-00 while the bottom drawing prints500-1011-00; no unique assembly part is promoted. START1 produces firmware TROUGH EJECT4, followed by synthetic occupancy transfer from11 to shooter17 and exit18. Physical ball count, sensor construction, connector routing, jam policy and travel are unresolved; this physical assembly stays unbound.
mechanisms.label: Ball trough kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Own item19 establishes post500-6752-04. Firmware output5 RIGHT RAMP BALL LOCK and inputs14/15/16 LOCKUP1-3 are candidate routes only; no actuation, physical association, default position or release sequence is proved.
mechanisms.label: Ball lock post
